terminal.description: A shell in your workspace. Build the bench and the waiting list here and run them, and watch when each repair ends.

tasks.title: Put one repair on both lists
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 1` in `src/lists.cpp`, write a function called `putOnBoth` that takes the bench and the waiting list, each as a reference to a `std::vector<std::shared_ptr<Repair>>`, a ticket as an `int` and an item as a reference to a `const std::string`, and gives nothing back. It makes one `Repair` with that ticket and item, owned by a `std::shared_ptr<Repair>`, and puts that one repair at the end of both lists.

Check calls `putOnBoth` with lists of its own and then checks that both lists hold the very same repair, and that its shared_ptr counts both of them as owners. It counts, with a `Repair` of its own, that every repair ends exactly once when the lists end.
nextSteps: Write the first line: `void`, the name, and the four parameters.
Make the repair once, with `std::make_shared<Repair>`, into a local `std::shared_ptr<Repair>`.
`push_back` that shared_ptr onto the bench, and onto the waiting list.
In `main`, put a repair on both lists and print its count of owners with `use_count()`.
hints: A `std::shared_ptr` can be copied: every copy is one more owner of the same repair, and they share one count. The repair ends when the count reaches 0.
Make the repair exactly once. Each `push_back` of the shared_ptr makes a copy of the owner, not of the repair.
The shape is `std::shared_ptr<Repair> repair = std::make_shared<Repair>(ticket, item); bench.push_back(repair); waiting.push_back(repair);`.

tasks.title: Let go of a repair
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 2`, write a function called `letGo` that takes a list as a reference to a `std::vector<std::shared_ptr<Repair>>` and a ticket as an `int`, and gives back a `bool`. It takes the repair with that ticket off the list, keeps the others in their order, and gives back `true`. When no repair on the list has that ticket, it changes nothing and gives back `false`. The repair itself ends only when nothing else holds it.

Check fills lists of its own, some repairs held by another list as well, and lets go of the first and a middle repair, a ticket that is not there, and one from an empty list. It checks what the list holds afterwards, and counts, with a `Repair` of its own, which repairs ended during the call: only one that nothing else held. Check builds this task with the library's guard, which stops a program that reads a vector past its end.
nextSteps: Write the first line, with the list taken by reference.
Walk the list with a counted loop, and compare each repair's ticket through `->`.
When it matches, `erase` that place and give back `true`.
After the loop, give back `false`. In `main`, let go of a repair from one list, then the other, and watch when it ends.
hints: A list of shared_ptrs holds a share in each repair. Taking a place off the list gives up that share, and nothing more.
No `delete` anywhere: the shared_ptrs decide when the repair ends. Erasing the place is enough, and the last owner to go ends the repair.
The shape is `for (std::size_t i = 0; i < list.size(); i++) { if (list[i]->getTicket() == ticket) { list.erase(list.begin() + i); return true; } } return false;`.

tasks.title: Count who holds a repair
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 3`, write a function called `ownersOf` that takes a list as a reference to a `const std::vector<std::shared_ptr<Repair>>` and a ticket as an `int`, and gives back a `long`: how many shared_ptrs own the repair with that ticket, as the shared_ptr counts them. When no repair on the list has that ticket, it gives back `0`.

Check sets up a bench and a waiting list that share some repairs, holds one repair once more itself, and asks `ownersOf` about tickets on one list, on both, on neither, and on an empty list.
nextSteps: Write the first line, with `long` in front of the name and the list as a `const` reference.
Loop over the list with `const std::shared_ptr<Repair>&`.
When the ticket matches, give back that shared_ptr's `use_count()`.
After the loop, give back `0`. In `main`, print the count before and after a list lets go.
hints: A shared_ptr knows how many owners share its repair. Every copy of a shared_ptr counts, as long as the copy lives, even one that only exists while a function runs.
Read the count through a reference, so the function holds no copy of its own while it counts. A loop variable without `&` is a copy, and adds one.
The shape is `for (const std::shared_ptr<Repair>& repair : list) { if (repair->getTicket() == ticket) { return repair.use_count(); } } return 0;`.
